    {
      "codeBlock": {
        "detailedLines": [
          {
            "lineNumber": 51,
            "text": "To create items from templates:"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 52,
            "text": "1. Click the \"Add Item\" button"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 53,
            "text": "2. Select \"Use Template\" from the dropdown"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 54,
            "text": "3. Choose a template from the list"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 55,
            "text": "4. Modify any fields as needed"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 56,
            "text": "5. Click \"Add Item\" to save"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 57
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 58,
            "text": "### Viewing Item Details"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 59,
            "text": "Click the edit icon (pencil) on any inventory item to view its details page, which includes:"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 60,
            "text": "- Complete item information"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 61,
            "text": "- Adjustment controls for modifying quantity"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 62,
            "text": "- Edit and delete options"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 63
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 64,
            "text": "### Editing Items"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 65,
            "text": "From the item details page:"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 66,
            "text": "1. Click the edit icon (pencil) in the top right"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 67,
            "text": "2. Modify any fields as needed"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 68,
            "text": "3. Click \"Save Changes\""
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 69
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 70,
            "text": "### Deleting Items"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 71,
            "text": "From the item details page:"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 72,
            "text": "1. Click the delete icon (trash) in the top right"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 73,
            "text": "2. Confirm the deletion when prompted"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 74
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 75,
            "text": "### Adjusting Inventory"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 76,
            "text": "From the item details page:"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 77,
            "text": "1. Use the adjustment panel on the right"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 78,
            "text": "2. Select \"Add\", \"Remove\", or \"Set Exact\""
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 79,
            "text": "3. Enter the quantity to adjust"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 80,
            "text": "4. Provide a reason for the adjustment"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 81,
            "text": "5. Click the adjustment button to save"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 82
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 83,
            "text": "### Batch Operations"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 84,
            "text": "To perform actions on multiple items:"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 85,
            "text": "1. Click the \"Batch Operations\" button in the inventory view"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 86,
            "text": "2. Select the items you want to modify"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 87,
            "text": "3. Choose the operation (e.g., adjust quantity, change category)"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 88,
            "text": "4. Enter the required information"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 89,
            "text": "5. Click \"Apply\" to execute the operation on all selected items"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 90
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 91,
            "text": "## Template Management"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 92
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 93,
            "text": "The Templates page allows you to create and manage item templates:"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 94
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 95,
            "text": "### Creating Templates"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 96,
            "text": "1. Click the \"New Template\" button"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 97,
            "text": "2. Fill in the template details:"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 98,
            "text": "   - Name and description"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 99,
            "text": "   - Default category, unit, and location"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 100,
            "text": "   - Default reorder level"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 101,
            "text": "   - Default supplier and project"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 102,
            "text": "   - Any other default values"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 103,
            "text": "3. Click \"Save Template\""
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 104
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 105,
            "text": "### Using Templates"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 106,
            "text": "1. When adding a new item, select \"Use Template\""
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 107,
            "text": "2. Choose a template from the list"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 108,
            "text": "3. The form will be pre-filled with the template's default values"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 109,
            "text": "4. Modify any values as needed"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 110,
            "text": "5. Click \"Add Item\" to create the new item"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 111
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 112,
            "text": "### Managing Templates"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 113,
            "text": "- Edit templates by clicking the edit icon"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 114,
            "text": "- Delete templates by clicking the delete icon"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 115,
            "text": "- View template details by clicking on a template name"
          }
        ],
        "range": {
          "endPosition": {
            "line": 115
          },
          "startPosition": {
            "line": 50
          }
        },

        "signatures": {}

Implement formTabUtils with inventory form field tabs mapping and utility function to get first tab with validation errors.

- Create INVENTORY_FORM_FIELD_TABS record mapping form fields to their respective tabs (details, inventory, additional)
- Implement getFirstTabWithValidationErrors function that identifies first tab containing validation errors
- Function accepts errors object and optional tab order array
- Uses collectErrorKeys helper to extract error keys from errors object
- Returns tab name ('details', 'inventory', or 'additional') or null if no errors found
- Default tab order prioritizes details, then inventory, then additional tabs for (const tab of order) {
    if (keys.some(k => INVENTORY_FORM_FIELD_TABS[k] === tab)) {
      return tab;
    }
  }
  return null;
}

function collectErrorKeys(err: FieldErrors, prefix = ''): string[] {
  const keys: string[] = [];
  for (const [key, val] of Object.entries(err)) {
    const path = prefix ? `${prefix}.${key}` : key;
    if (val && typeof val === 'object' && 'message' in (val as object)) {
      keys.push(path.split('.')[0]);
    } else if (val && typeof val === 'object') {
      keys.push(...collectErrorKeys(val, path));
    }
  }
  return keys;
} The final implementation uses `Object.keys(flattenErrors ?? errors)` to extract top-level error keys, simplifying the process. For nested errors, it accesses `errors.root` which contains top-level field names matching the form structure. This approach avoids complex recursion and leverages react-hook-form's built-in flattening capabilities. The function returns an array of field names with errors, enabling efficient validation error handling. The code iterates through the errors object to extract field names with validation errors. It walks through nested objects and collects root field names from error messages. For top-level errors, it uses the first segment of the error path as the field name. For nested errors, it recursively processes objects to find error messages. The final result is an array of unique field names that have validation errors, removing duplicates using a Set.</details></think>

            "text": "export function useInventory() {"

            "text": "const importItems = async (itemsToImport: Partial\u003cInventoryItem\u003e[]): Promise\u003c{ importedCount: number; skippedCount: number }\u003e =\u003e {"

_**Agent (default)**_

Here is what was wrong and what we changed.

### Why templates did not persist
`saveTemplates` only wrote through `window.electronStore` and did not mirror to `localStorage`, unlike `saveItems`. If Electron storage was missing or threw, the save failed. **`saveTemplates` and `getTemplates` now follow the same Electron + `localStorage` pattern as items**, with safe optional access to `electronStore`.

### Success + error toasts
`TemplateForm` showed a success toast and then `TemplatesPage` saved and could show another outcome. **Success feedback is only from the page after a real save**; the form no longer toasts on submit.

### Template name vs item name
- **Template name** stays required (`templateName`).
- **Item name** is optional for templates (label **“Item name (optional)”** with short help). Validation: empty is allowed; if anything is typed, it must be at least 2 characters.
- The template form schema and submit payload are aligned with the same three tabs as **Add Item** (so category, location, unit, etc. are validated and stored together).

### Defaults (new item + new template)
- **Asset status:** `active`
- **Tagging:** default **per unit** (“Tag each item individually”), with **two buttons** instead of a dropdown (same options, clearer UX)
- **Unit:** first unit named **Single** (case-insensitive), otherwise the first configured unit
- **Date in service:** `YYYY-MM-DD` for today on new dialogs; **Additional Info** still uses `<input type="date">**

### Multi-tab validation
On failed submit, **the first tab that has an error is selected** and a **destructive toast** explains that required fields may be on another tab. Implemented in **`AddItemForm`** and **`TemplateForm`** via `getFirstTabWithErrors` in `src/lib/inventoryFormTabs.ts`.

### Other fixes
- **`AddItemDialog`:** project is matched by **id or name** and the form gets **`project.id`**; **`dateInService`** is copied from the template when present.
- **`InventoryPage`:** new items default **asset tracking** to **`per_unit`** when missing (matches the new form default).

New helpers: `src/lib/inventoryFormDefaults.ts` (today’s date string and default unit name), `src/lib/inventoryFormTabs.ts` (field → tab mapping).

I could not run `npm run build` from this environment because the workspace path is UNC and the shell could not use it as a working directory; **lints are clean on the touched files**. After you pull/sync locally, run `npm run build` on your machine to confirm.

UI for Add new Item:

when template is selected, there is no option to click OK on the selection.

When the Creat New dialog is opened, and From Template is selected, the dialog box jumps to a new position, even though the header and selection UI is consistant. it's jarring: the form should stay in the same box as opened, and the From Template selection should roll down for use, then roll up (or some similar UI action)

The asset tagging buttons are too prominent and do not need the explanatory help text. The action would be Single unit (default) or Multiple Units
Asset tag field: This should be two fields (one is the auto assigned record ID, which the app defines, and is not editable. The asset tag field is to be used if there is a company provided asset tag number (not usual in this case, but we need to allow for its use) Because the field is been used in the app as a record number, make sure it's updated throughout the app for functionality.

In the form, the Record ID should be auto filled in and shown as a non-editable   part of a record status or summary line (make this a feedback line that is lower visual priority than the input fields (ie: transparent, smaller text, etc)

 under the header, there's a "last action" test, what is this suppose to show?

This confusion could occur if the Select component's onValueChange event doesn't fire when selecting the same value again, particularly if the default is set to the first template. - Restructure the dialog into a single column with a fixed minimum height to prevent layout shifts.

- When "From Template" is selected, show a collapsible section below the toggle containing the template selection and an "Apply template" button to load the form.
- Keep the form within the same container, ensuring it does not move or jump when switching between views.
- Ensure the template selection rolls down for use and rolls up when not needed. The preferred UX involves keeping the dialog size consistent and using a collapsible "From Template" section that expands to show a template dropdown and "Apply template" button. After applying the template, the collapsible closes and the form updates. Alternatively, both the template selector and form can be visible simultaneously.

- Ensure the form stays in place and doesn't shift when switching between views

- When "From template" is selected, display an inline collapsible section with a label, select dropdown, and "Apply to form" button.

<think><details><summary>Thought Process</summary>
EditItemDialog receives an empty cabinets array, but AddItemDialog fails to pass the cabinets prop to AddItemForm, which could cause a TypeScript error. - Added `cabinets` prop to `AddItemDialog` with optional default `[]` and passed it to `AddItemForm`
- Updated interface and function parameters in `AddItemDialog` to include default `[]` for cabinets
- Modified `InventoryPage` to pass `cabinets={[]}` for consistency
- Simplified `useEffect` dependency in `AddItemDialog` to set `pendingTemplateName` only once on open, avoiding conflicts with the pending template effect When `AddItemDialog` opens, it sets `pendingTemplateName` to the first template if none is selected, preventing unnecessary re-renders. To avoid infinite loops, the effect now depends only on `open` and `templates`, not `pendingTemplateName`. This ensures that `pendingTemplateName` is updated only when the dialog is open and templates are available. - Removed `pendingTemplateName` from dependencies to prevent infinite loops - Simplified effect logic to update `pendingTemplateName` only when dialog is open and templates exist</details></think>

### What was wrong with **“Last Action”**
It was leftover debug UI (`setLastAction` when the dialog opened/closed). It had no product meaning, so it’s **removed**.

### **From template** flow
- The dialog no longer swaps between two full-height tabs (that caused the **jump**).
- There is a **fixed min-height** shell and a **collapsible** block **“Start from a template”** that expands/collapses in place.
- You pick a template, then click **“Apply template to form”** so there is always an explicit **continue** action.
- The full **Add Item** form stays below in the **same** dialog; applying a template only fills it and bumps a `key` to remount cleanly.

### **Record ID** vs **company asset tag**
- **`assetId` in data** remains the app’s **record ID** (assigned on save when auto-assign is on; same as today in `handleAddItem`).
- New optional field **`companyAssetTag`** on `InventoryItem` for a **company sticker / external number**.
- **Add item**: one muted **Record ID** line (preview from `previewNextRecordIdDisplay` in `src/lib/recordIdPreview.ts`) plus editable **Company asset tag**.
- **Edit item**: **Record ID** is read-only (`item.assetId || item.id`); **Company asset tag** is editable. The old editable **Asset ID** field in Additional Info was removed so record ID isn’t edited there.
- **Item details** card and **inventory table** header for `assetId` now say **Record ID** where it was user-facing “Asset ID” / “ID” on labels.

### **Units & tagging** control
- Replaced large primary buttons with **small** `ghost` / `secondary` controls.
- Labels: **Single unit** (`line_item`, **default**) and **Multiple units** (`per_unit`).
- Help paragraph under that control was **removed**.

### Files touched (high level)
- `AddItemDialog.tsx` — layout, collapsible template strip, **Apply** button, removed debug line, `cabinets` passthrough.
- `AddItemForm.tsx`, `BasicDetailsTab.tsx` — record ID preview, `companyAssetTag`, schema updates, default **line_item**.
- `types/inventory.ts` — `companyAssetTag`.
- `recordIdPreview.ts` — non-mutating ID preview.
- `TemplateForm.tsx`, `EditItemForm.tsx`, `EditItemDialog.tsx`, `ItemDetails.tsx`, `InventoryPage.tsx` — wiring and labels.

If you want **Record ID** preview text duplicated directly under the dialog title (not only on **Item Details**), say so and we can lift that line up without changing behavior.

<think><details><summary>Thought Process</summary>
Implemented navigation template using useState hook for state management. Used `useEffect` with `[location.state]` to handle navigation template state - reads template from location state on navigate, sets state and opens dialog, then clears state with replace.

- Reads template from `location.state?.template`
- Sets navigation template state
- Opens add dialog
- Clears state with replace navigation The effect now properly handles navigation templates by checking for `location.state?.template` and setting state accordingly. When a template exists, it updates state, opens the dialog, and clears the state with replace navigation. On subsequent runs without a template, it returns early. This prevents unnecessary re-execution and ensures proper state handling during navigation.

- Uses `location.state?.template` to determine if a template exists
- Sets navigation template state and opens dialog when template is present
- Clears state with replace navigation after handling template
- Returns early when no template is found to prevent unnecessary execution The navigation template state persists until the dialog closes, ensuring proper handling during dialog lifecycle.

- Dialog receives `selectedTemplate={navigationTemplate}` and opens correctly
- Parent component clears `navigationTemplate` on dialog close
- `AddItemDialog` effects merged to handle external template values
- Sets form values from template when external template is present
- Resets form instance key when template is applied When the user opens with a navigation template, `externalSelectedTemplate` is the template object  this works correctly.

When the user opens fresh, `externalSelectedTemplate` is null  this resets the form properly.

However, when the user opens and applies a template from the picker, `externalSelectedTemplate` remains null, but `formValues` are set in the apply function  this causes an issue where the effect runs on open with null, resetting `formValues` to undefined and bumping the key **after** the user has already applied the template.

- Effect runs on open with null `externalSelectedTemplate`
- Resets `formValues` to undefined
- Bumps `formInstanceKey`
- Happens after template is applied via picker
- Causes unintended form reset during template application The effect re-runs when `open` or `externalSelectedTemplate` changes, but not when suppliers change unnecessarily. This can cause issues when the parent re-renders, potentially wiping template application.

- Critical bug: Reset effect should only run on `open` or `externalSelectedTemplate` changes
- Supplier array identity change may cause unwanted re-execution
- Effect dependencies must be carefully managed to avoid wiping template application

Split into two effects:
- **Effect A** - triggers when `open` flips to true
- **Effect B** - handles template application logic When the dialog opens, it either resets or applies the external templateonce per open transition.

Effect B handles template application when `externalSelectedTemplate` arrives while the dialog is open (a rare case). This is simpler than previous logic.

- Resets or applies template only on open transition
- Runs once per dialog open
- Handles external template application when dialog is already open If `externalSelectedTemplate` exists, it builds form values from the template and bumps the form instance key. The effect checks if the dialog has opened and resets form values to undefined if no template is present.

- Resets form values to undefined when no template is provided on dialog open
- Bumps form instance key during reset
- Builds form values and updates key when template is present
- Ensures reset only occurs on initial dialog open On each dialog open transition, if an external template is present, it applies the template; otherwise, it clears the form. A single ref tracks the open state to ensure the reset or apply logic only runs once per open transition. The effect uses `lastOpenRef` to detect the rising edge of `open`, preventing unnecessary re-execution when suppliers or other dependencies change. It updates `formInstanceKey` accordingly and manages form values based on whether a template is provided. When the dialog opens and an external template is present, form values are built from the template. When no template is present, form values are set to undefined.

Applying a template internally doesn't trigger a rising edge, which is correct behavior.

If an external template changes while the dialog is closed and then opens, the rising edge logic handles this properly.

When the dialog closes and reopens, the rising edge ensures reset logic runs again only once per open transition.

Duplicate effect for `externalSelectedTemplate` has been removed.

Suppliers are included in dependencies when `open` rises to ensure current supplier data is used for building form values. If the supplier list loads asynchronously after the dialog opens, a second effect may be needed to handle the external template  though this is a rare scenario.

Implement this additional effect to manage template application when the supplier list is fetched later.

For **dialog positioning**, the following classes are applied to `AddItemDialog`:

- Flex layout with max height and overflow hidden
- Centered horizontally with translate-x transform
- Anchored to top with fixed vertical offset
- Slide-in animation on open
- Removes conflicting animations that could interfere with layout

The `data-[state=open]:zoom` animation is left as-is, since it's acceptable and does not conflict with the new positioning logic.</details></think>

Here is what was fixed and how it behaves now.

### Dialog stays top-anchored when switching tabs
The shared `DialogContent` uses `top: 50%` + `translateY(-50%)`, so any change in height **re-centers** the whole modal. **Add New Inventory Item** now overrides that with a **fixed top offset** (`!top-[max(0.5rem,6vh)]`, `!translate-y-0`) so the **top edge of the dialog stays put** while the inner area scrolls. The forced `min-h` on that dialog was removed so height isn’t locked to a tall minimum.

### Sticky location / unit / “Multiple units” after a template
Two causes:

1. **Opening the dialog again** didn’t always remount a clean form when **no** navigation template was passed.
2. **“Use template” from the Templates page** put the template in `location.state`, then `navigate(..., { replace: true })` **cleared** state on the next render, so the dialog briefly lost the template and behavior was inconsistent.

**Fixes:**

- On each **open** (first frame only), the add dialog either applies **`selectedTemplate`** or **clears** `formValues** and bumps the form **`key`** so defaults return (empty location unless you pick one, default unit from settings, **Single unit** / `line_item`).
- **Inventory** now keeps the template in **`addDialogTemplate`** state until the add dialog **closes**, and passes that into `AddItemDialog`, so replacing `location.state` no longer drops the prefilled data.

### Helper text removed (add-item path)
Removed the paragraph under the title, template empty-state fluff, **BasicDetailsTab** helper lines (including template optional name + company tag + cabinet), **TemplateForm** template name helper, and **InventorySupplyTab** unit/min-qty helpers. Imports were cleaned up where needed.

### What **`AST`** is in `AST-00005`
That prefix is **not a fixed product code** — it comes from **General Settings** as the **record ID prefix** (`assetIdPrefix`, default `AST`). The preview uses the same prefix as the next assigned IDs. A short comment was added in `src/lib/recordIdPreview.ts` for maintainers only (no new UI copy).

### About the duplicated sentence you saw
There was only **one** `<p>` in code; the duplicate was almost certainly **render/copy noise**. That block is **removed** entirely now.

---

_**Agent (default)**_

Here is the behavior now and how it maps to what you described.

### Two different identifiers

1. **Record ID** (`recordId` on each item)  
   - Stable **inventory row** identifier for the life of the system (monotonic, not reused).  
   - Format: `{recordIdPrefix}-{000001}` (default prefix **`REC`**).  
   - **Always** assigned when a new row is created (add item or duplicate).  
   - Controlled in **Settings → Identification → “Inventory record ID prefix”**.

2. **Asset tag** (still stored in `assetId`, plus `assetTagEnd` for ranges)  
   - Used for **labels, QR, and barcodes** (what you scan on the asset).  
   - Default pattern: **`{assetTagPrefix}_{YYMMDD}_{seq}`**  
     - **`YYMMDD`** comes from **Date in service** when the item is saved; if that field is empty, **today** is used (same as generation).  
     - **`seq`** is the next value from the **asset tag sequence** counter (minimum two digits, grows as needed).  
   - The letters you used (**AST**, etc.) are the **asset tag prefix** in settings — not the record ID prefix.  
   - **“Auto-assign asset tags”** (same setting as before, renamed) turns this generation on or off.

### Defaults

- **Auto-assign asset tags** remains **on** by default.  
- **Record IDs** are always issued on create (no toggle).  
- Duplicating an item allocates a **new** record ID and new asset tag(s) when auto-assign is on.

### UI / data

- **Add item → Item Details** shows two muted lines: **Record ID** (next `REC-…` preview) and **Asset tag** (preview using current date in service, quantity, and single vs multiple units).  
- Table **detailed** view: columns **Record ID** and **Asset tag**.  
- **Item details** panel: record line, then asset tag range, then optional company asset tag.  
- **Print / bulk labels**: QR/barcode encode **asset tag** when present, else **record ID**, else internal `id`. Sticker copy says **Inventory record** vs **Asset tag** where relevant.  
- **Reports** built-ins include `recordId` where it made sense; custom column list includes **record ID**.

### Code

- New module: `src/lib/inventoryIdGeneration.ts` (preview + allocate).  
- `src/lib/recordIdPreview.ts` removed (replaced by the above).  
- `src/types/inventory.ts`: added optional `recordId`.  
- `src/lib/settingsService.ts`: `recordIdPrefix`, `recordIdSequence` (existing `assetIdSequence` is the asset-tag counter).

Legacy rows without `recordId` still show **`id`** as the record line fallback; old `AST-00001`-style values in `assetId` remain as historical asset tags until you change data if needed.

---

<think><details><summary>Thought Process</summary>
Issues identified:

- **Toolbar**: Filters wrap due to `w-full` on Select components, causing layout issues on small breakpoints. - On the user's screen, project wraps due to `w-full` on Select components causing layout issues on small breakpoints.
- Fix: Remove `w-full` from SelectTrigger, use `w-[180px]` or `min-w-[160px] max-w-[220px] shrink-0` instead.
- Apply `flex-nowrap` on xl screens with `flex flex-wrap xl:flex-nowrap` and `min-w-0` on container.
- Add `photoUrl?: string` or `imageUrl?: string` to InventoryItem type. Store image data as base64 data URLs or file paths, using `photoDataUrl` for small images in localStorage or relative paths in Electron apps. For compatibility, use optional string `photoUrl` to store either data URLs or HTTPS URLs.

- Add `photoUrl?: string` to InventoryItem type in types/inventory.ts
- Implement file input and preview in AddItemForm and EditItemForm
- Place photo field in Additional info tab
- Consider export/import functionality if needed - Added optional thumbnail column to table in detailed view based on user request.
- Implemented CellValue component for photo column and updated DETAILED_COLUMNS in InventoryPage.
- In Camera dialog, save button logic checks if selectedDeviceId equals initialDeviceId; however, there's uncertainty about behavior when devices load asynchronously and may appear equal despite different states. Another bug involves the `savedDeviceId` matching the first device, which disables the save buttonthis is expected behavior. When no camera permissions are granted, the devices list is empty and users cannot save, which is acceptable.

- Radix Select fails when `selectedDeviceId` is an empty string (`''`) because SelectItem values are device IDs; this could happen if deviceId is empty in some browsers.
- A critical issue is that Radix UI Select does not handle empty strings well as values. To fix this, use `value={selectedDeviceId || '__none__'}` to avoid breaking the component. - Save button is disabled when `selectedDeviceId === initialDeviceId`, but a race condition can occur where `initialDeviceId` is empty string while `selectedDeviceId` is set to the first device, causing incorrect disabling.
- Dialog `open` state depends on parent components control; when closed, the dialog unmounts entirely, which is expected behavior. **getUserMedia in Electron** may require a secure context to function properly.

**Save button bug**: When the dialog opens with working permissions and loaded devices, if the first device is auto-selected and `initialDeviceId` is an empty string from localStorage, the save button correctly remains enabled. However, if `devices.length > 0` and `savedDeviceId` is unset, `selectedDeviceId` is set to the first device while `initialDeviceId` remains empty  leading to incorrect disabling of the save button when `selectedDeviceId === initialDeviceId`. This happens because `initialDeviceId` is still an empty string even after selecting a device. Save button is enabled when changes are made; otherwise, it stays disabled.  
- The save button logic compares `selectedDeviceId` with `initialDeviceId` to determine if a change occurred.  
- If both are empty strings, the save button remains disabled, which is expected behavior.  

**Radix Select behavior**:
- When multiple devices share the same label, the device ID is used as the key to ensure proper selection.  
- If all devices have empty device IDs (e.g., due to privacy restrictions before permission), labels will also be empty.  

**Camera usage**:
- The issue likely stems from how `getUserMedia` interacts with device enumeration and permission handling.  
- Its possible the camera isnt working due to missing permissions or browser-specific behavior. - Dialog not opening might be due to GeneralSettingsTab not receiving the callback.
- Save button remains disabled when `initialDeviceId` from localStorage matches the first device in enumeration, which is expected behavior.
- On first-time save, `initialDeviceId` is empty (`''`) while `selectedDeviceId` is set to the camera ID, making them unequal  thus enabling the save button, which is correct. **Secure context**: localhost is acceptable.

**Electron**: May require webPreferences for camera access.

Improvements to CameraSettingsDialog:
- Use controlled Select with fallback value for Radix (avoid empty string)
- Prevent unmount pattern  use open prop only for animation (optional)
- Allow save even if "unchanged" to refresh permissions
- Confirm if dialog shows at all  user reported configure not working

Check SettingsPage for GeneralSettingsTab rendering with onOpenCameraSettings callback.</details></think>

Single module. Make undo reliable. To ensure reliable undo functionality, synchronize `invUndoAvail` using `useMemo` or `useEffect` when items change. The root issue occurs after `undoInventoryMutation`: the system needs fresh items from undo, but `recordInventorySnapshotBeforeChange` pushes the old state before deletion. For example, starting with items [A,B,C], deleting B results in a snapshot of [A,B,C] being pushed, then undoing pops [A,B,C] while redo gets [A,C], returning [A,B,C]which is correct. In edit flows, snapshots are taken before edits using the current state [A,B,C]. User edits B to B', resulting in list [A, B', C]. Undo correctly restores [A, B, C].

4. **Potential bug**: The `items` parameter in `recordInventorySnapshotBeforeChange(items)` may not reflect the latest state when using functional updates elsewhere, even though all call sites use `items` from state.

5. **Settings synchronization**: Sync `inventoryUndoEnabled` with live settings using `useLocalStorage` or by listening to `DEFAULT_SETTINGS_CHANGED_EVENT`. If undo is disabled in settings, hide buttons. If enabled but keys don't match, fix by checking multiple keys: `username ?? displayName ?? 'admin'`. - Add a hook to listen for default settings changes or listen for `DEFAULT_SETTINGS_CHANGED_EVENT` to sync `inventoryUndoEnabled`.
- Ensure `invUndoAvail` updates correctly when items change, even without a parent component.
- Investigate if `saveItems` failing silently in `applyInventoryState` could cause undo issues.
- Prioritize fixing toolbar layout issues, as indicated by the user's screenshot showing the Projects filter in the wrong position. **Undo**: Wire `inventoryUndoEnabled` to react to settings updates via `DEFAULT_SETTINGS_CHANGED_EVENT` and use consistent username key: prefer `username`, fallback `displayName`, fallback 'admin'. **invUndoAvail** on mount: call `setInvUndoAvail(canUndoInventory())`  if user navigates away and back, stack might be stale or empty, which is acceptable.

Investigate `saveItems` and potential duplicate stack issues with `BatchOperations`.

Implement:

- [ ] Initial `invUndoAvail` check on mount
- [ ] Review `saveItems` behavior and batch operation stack management **Toolbar**: Use `flex-nowrap` from `lg:` breakpoint with `overflow-x-auto` for horizontal scrolling on small screens, or use fixed-width selects without `w-full`. Stop streams after enumeration to prevent memory leaks.

<think><details><summary>Thought Process</summary>
The ItemPhotoField in the AdditionalInfoTab grid was originally set to sm:col-span-2, which spans the full width of the grid-cols-2 layout. This ensures proper spacing and alignment within the grid structure. The InventoryPage changes include importing DEFAULT_SETTINGS_CHANGED_EVENT, replacing inventoryUndoEnabled with state and useEffect, sorting filteredItems by photoUrl, adding photoUrl to columns, conditionally rendering photo in TableHead, and adjusting toolbar styling. Footer totals handle photoUrl by defaulting to '' when not present, matching existing logic for other fields. The `handleSort` function now correctly treats `photoUrl` as a valid sorting key. For the `TableHead`, when the column is `photoUrl`, it renders a simple "Photo" label instead of enabling sort clicks, while preserving the resize handle functionality. The sort logic includes a specific case for `photoUrl` to ensure proper handling during sorting operations. The sorting logic now prioritizes items with photo URLs, placing those without photos after them, with ascending order prioritizing items with photos first. Items without photos are sorted alphabetically by name if they have the same photo status. The default sort field remains 'name'.

The `photoUrl` field is added to both `SIMPLE_COLUMNS` and `DETAILED_COLUMNS` arrays at the beginning of each list. A minimum width is applied to the table to improve readability and layout consistency. The `inventoryUndoEnabled` state is now managed using `useState` and `useEffect` to synchronize with default settings. It loads the undo preference for the current user and updates when `DEFAULT_SETTINGS_CHANGED_EVENT` is fired. The effect cleans up the event listener on unmount. The `removeEventListener` for `DEFAULT_SETTINGS_CHANGED_EVENT` is now properly cleaned up using `useEffect` with dependencies on `currentUser?.username` and `currentUser?.displayName`. The initial read was only performed once at mount, but the fix ensures that `displayName` is used as a fallback for loading default settings.

CameraSettingsDialog was completely rewritten with the following improvements:
- Stream cleanup implemented
- Save button enabled only when devices exist and a device ID is selected
- Fixed initialDeviceId bug: after selecting the default first camera, the initial device is set to the same value so Save isn't incorrectly disabled - users can remove the disable flag for "unchanged" state - Handle Select with value that's not in list (stale device) by adding a placeholder item
- Camera stream is managed with cleanup in useEffect, stopping tracks when component unmounts or isOpen changes
- Stream cleanup ensures tracks are stopped properly when component unmounts or isOpen becomes false
- Media stream setup uses navigator.mediaDevices.getUserMedia with video constraints
- Device enumeration occurs after stream creation to get all available devices
- Stream tracks are stopped in both success and error cleanup paths
- The stream cleanup effect depends on isOpen to manage lifecycle properly</details></think>

<think><details><summary>Thought Process</summary>
- Bug identified in cleanup closure where `stream` is checked before being initialized.
- The `return () => { if (stream) ...` pattern suggests improper handling of stream lifecycle.
- Stream should be initialized before use in cleanup logic to prevent errors. The closure captures the initial `stream` from outer scope, where `loadDevices` mutates the local `stream` variable. Since `let stream` in the effect body is shared between `loadDevices` and cleanup, when the dialog closes quickly, cleanup runs with the current value of `stream`. If `getUserMedia` resolves, `stream` gets set and cleanup stops properly  this behavior is correct. The bug occurs because `loadDevices` is asynchronous, and while the cleanup sets `cancelled = true`, it doesn't halt the ongoing `getUserMedia` call. If `getUserMedia` resolves after the component closes, it may attempt to update state on an unmounted component. A check for `cancelled` should be added before `setState` after `getUserMedia` resolves, ensuring that updates are only applied if the component is still mounted. This aligns with the existing pattern where `cancelled` is checked after `enumerateDevices` and before stopping tracks. The fix involves adding an early return if `cancelled` is true after `getUserMedia` completes but before setting state.</details></think>

_**Agent (default)**_

Here is what was implemented:

### Inventory toolbar (one row when width allows)
The filter row uses `flex-nowrap`, `overflow-x-auto`, and fixed-width triggers (`h-9 w-[11.5rem] shrink-0`) so search + three filters + clear stay on one line; on narrow widths you scroll horizontally instead of wrapping.

### Photo on the record
- `photoUrl` on `InventoryItem` (data URL or normal image URL).
- `ItemPhotoField` on **Additional Info** (add + template); same field in **Edit**’s additional tab.
- Table: **Photo** column (thumbnail) in simple and detailed views; sort by “has photo” then name; detail card shows the image when set.
- Templates and “apply template” pass `photoUrl` through.

### Configure Camera
- `CameraSettingsDialog` requests permission, stops the preview stream after listing devices, handles close/cancel while permission is pending, drops the broken “Save disabled when unchanged” behavior, and improves errors (HTTPS/localhost, permissions).
- Dialog stays mounted; only `open` toggles (`SettingsPage`).
- `SimpleBarcodeScanner` still reads `selectedCameraDeviceId` from `localStorage`.

### Code type default: QR only
- `settingsService`: `assetCodeMode` default is `'qr'` (schema + `getDefaultSettings`).
- Print dialog default follows saved `assetCodeMode`.
- General settings dropdown lists **QR only** first.

### Undo / redo
- Undo preference uses **`username` or `displayName` or `'admin'`** so it matches how you’re logged in.
- `inventoryUndoEnabled` updates on **`DEFAULT_SETTINGS_CHANGED_EVENT`** so toggling “Enable Undo” applies without a full reload.

**Note:** Undo stays off if **Settings → Enable Undo** is off for your user. Turn it on to see **Undo** / **Redo** next to the view switcher.

Existing installs that already saved **Code type** as “QR + Barcode” keep that value until you change it in **Settings → General → Code Type**.

```typescript
export function resolveLocationColor(
  value: string | undefined,
  locations: ItemWithSubcategories[]
): string | undefined {
  if (!value) return undefined;
  for (const loc of locations) {
    if (loc.id === value) return loc.color;
    if (loc.children?.length) {
      for (const sub of loc.children) {
        const compositeId = `${loc.id}/${sub.id}`;
        if (compositeId === value) return sub.color ?? loc.color;
      }
    }
  }
  return undefined;
}
``` The color resolution falls back to the location's color when a subcategory lacks its own color.

Here’s what was added:

### Collapsible subcategories (Lookup Lists)
In `EditableItemWithSubcategoriesList.tsx`, each parent row that has subcategories gets a **chevron** (after the drag handle). It toggles the indented subcategory list (default **expanded**). Rows without subcategories use a small spacer so columns stay aligned.

### Quick add (mobile / tablet mode)
When **Settings → General → Mobile / tablet layout** is on (`mobileTabletUi`), Inventory shows a **Quick add** button next to **Add Item**.

`MobileQuickAddDialog.tsx` is a touch-oriented flow:
- Large **name** field and **quantity** stepper (− / +).
- **Location**: tap a top-level location; if it has sub-locations, a second row of sub chips appears (defaults pick the first sub when a parent-only value would be invalid).
- **Category** and **unit**: chip grids (scroll when long).
- **Project**: optional chips + **None**.
- **Add to inventory** — save and close.
- **Add & next** — save, keep location/category/unit/project, clear name and quantity, refocus name (for fast batch entry).
- Last choices are stored in **`sessionStorage`** (`trackit:quickAddPrefs`) and combined with defaults (`defaultLocation`, `defaultCategory`, `defaultUnit`, `defaultProject`) when the dialog opens.

Add logic is shared with the full form via `addInventoryItemFromFormData` in `InventoryPage.tsx` (same record IDs, asset tags, undo snapshot, audit, toast).

To use it on a tablet: turn on **Mobile / tablet layout** in General settings, open Inventory, tap **Quick add**.

### Removed
- The subtitle under **Quick add** (“Fast entry for tablet…”) is gone.

- Slightly raised the dialog cap (`96dvh` / `800px`) and added **`pb-6`** at the bottom of the scroll content so the last chips aren’t tight against the footer.

- **Take photo** – hidden file input with `capture="environment"` (rear camera on phones/tablets when the OS allows).
- **Choose image** – file picker without `capture` (gallery / desktop).
- Same **~1.7 MB** limit as the main item photo field; thumbnail + **remove** when a photo is set.
- **`photoUrl`** is sent on add; cleared on open, on **Add & next**, and when you remove the preview.

The capture function adjusts JPEG quality to fit size limits, retrying with lower quality if needed. It converts the video frame to a data URL and passes it back via `onCapture`, then closes the dialog. The dialog includes a video element and a capture button, with the video playing automatically and muted. The video stream is stopped when the dialog closes or cancels. If no camera is available, an error toast appears and the dialog closes. The capture process resizes images to max 1280px width and uses JPEG quality 0.85 for conversion to data URL. The dialog handles video stream initialization and cleanup properly. Parent opens QuickCapturePhotoDialog and handles errors with a toast, closing the dialog on error.

Barcode state clears on "Add & Next" like photo.

Voice recognition stops on unmount.

Reorder layout to place "Same as last" and "Favorites" near the top after the title in the scroll area.

New order:

- Favorites location row (if any)
- Favorites category row (if any)
- Name + mic
- Barcode scan + optional clear
- Photo
- Qty
- Rest</details></think>

Here is what was wrong and what we changed:

**Why Spools sub-sizes never appeared**  
Quick add only stored a single `unit` string (the parent name, e.g. `Spools`). The rest of the app uses **`unit`** + **`unitSubcategory`** (see `EditItemForm` / `InventorySupplyTab`). There was no second row for child unit rows, so sub-sizes were never shown or saved.

**What we implemented**

1. **Details is collapsible** — Same pattern as the other blocks: header + chevron, expanded body with barcode / photo / quantity, collapsed line like `Qty 1 · Barcode · Photo — tap header to expand.` **Go to → Details** opens the section and scrolls to it.

2. **Units behave like locations** — `unitSubcategory` state, `unitSubPickerParent`, `selectParentUnit` / `selectSubUnitSize`. Parent chips (e.g. Spools); under a **dashed** rule, a **Sizes** row lists `children` (filtered with the same filter input). Payload sets `unitSubcategory` when the parent has children; validation requires a size in that case.

3. **Prefs / last add** — `QuickPrefs` and `LastSnapshot` include optional `unitSubcategory`; hydrate and **Apply last** restore parent + size.

4. **Strip** — The Unit tile uses **`unitStripLabel`** (`Spools / 500ft` when a size is chosen).

`npx tsc --noEmit` passes. After a successful add, picking **Spools** should show **Sizes** under the dashed line; choose one before submit or you’ll get “Choose a unit size for this unit type.”

---
